fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Paul says their "…abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity." (2 Corinthians 8:2) Think about that. Deep poverty and a terrible ordeal, and the giving still came pouring out.

Oh, friend, it's the other way around. Paul testifies that "…they gave according to their ability and even beyond it." (2 Corinthians 8:3) So they didn't stop at what they could afford. They kept going past it. Not a cent more? These folks went PAST that line.

Close to how some of us feel about chores, baker, but that's not what the verse says. They pleaded for "…the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints." (2 Corinthians 8:4) They saw it as a gift to be part of. A burden is something you'd hand off, and they were pleading to take part.
That's right, baker. Paul says they "…gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, through the will of God." (2 Corinthians 8:5) The Lord came first. Their giving to Paul's team came after that.

Not quite, baker. Prophets don't show up in this verse at all. Paul says they "…gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, through the will of God." (2 Corinthians 8:5) Before Paul's team got a turn, the Lord got the first one. I'd have been checking the line for prophets too, so no shame there.

Right on, baker. Paul says, "…I am testing the sincerity of your love through the earnestness of others." (2 Corinthians 8:8) He isn't handing down an order. He's checking whether their love is the real thing. Love that's real shows up in what we do.

Good thought, friend, but loyalty to Titus isn't what Paul is testing. He says, "…I am testing the sincerity of your love through the earnestness of others." (2 Corinthians 8:8) What's on the table is the sincerity of the Corinthians' love.

Faith is on Paul's list of things they excel in, baker, so that was a smart pick. But he says, "…I am testing the sincerity of your love through the earnestness of others." (2 Corinthians 8:8) The word on the test is love, and the question is whether it's sincere. Faith already passed in verse 7.

Yes, baker! Paul says, "Now finish the work, so that you may complete it with the same eager desire, according to your means." (2 Corinthians 8:11) They started strong last year. Now it's time to cross the finish line.

You got it, baker. Paul says, "It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality." (2 Corinthians 8:13) The aim is a fair balance. He doesn't want one side carrying all of it.

Honor's a nice word, friend, but it's not the one here. Paul says, "It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality." (2 Corinthians 8:13) I'd say he's after a level table, with nobody stuck holding more than their share. Honor can't even out a load, but equality can.

Whoa, friend, Paul isn't painting that picture. He says, "…your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need." (2 Corinthians 8:14) The way he puts it, it's a two-way street. The others' surplus meets the Corinthians' need in turn.
